_what: v05 SFX library (REVISION_v05.md G9 + S, client doc 2.7). Lanes name these in hyperframes/<composition>/cues.json; tools/build_tesseract_audio.py places them.
format: 48 kHz, 24-bit PCM WAV; mono unless the sound moves in the stereo field (Tesseract plays a mono file at full level on both channels)
levels: Each file is written at its default level: its sample peak = default_peak_dbfs (pre-master; the assembly's master gain, about -1 dB, comes on top). The audio build plays a cue at default_peak_dbfs, or at the cue's gain_db (an absolute sample-peak level in dBFS, capped at -4 dBFS) when the cue gives one. Variant sets are loudness-matched, the loudest at the default.
align: start = the file's first sound on the cue frame (leading silence trimmed to 1 ms); peak = the file's sample peak (peak_s) on the frame; end = the file's last sample at the frame's start.
classes: pop/hit/tone: never touched by dropouts. sweep: transitions on cuts. riser/ambience (dropout_mute true): silenced inside every cues.json `dropouts` window they overlap (2-6 f before a big word), like the music bed would be.

tick.recipe: synthesized (numpy): tick_1: band-passed noise 2500-7000 Hz (decay 4.0 ms) + 1850 Hz sine (decay 6 ms), 0.4 ms attack, 60 ms | tick_2: band-passed noise 3200-9000 Hz (decay 3.5 ms) + 2650 Hz sine (decay 5 ms), 0.4 ms attack, 60 ms | tick_3: band-passed noise 1500-5000 Hz (decay 5.0 ms) + 1200 Hz sine (decay 8 ms) + 2400 Hz sine (decay 4 ms), 0.4 ms attack, 60 ms
tick.notes: Every caption word that is not key/hero (cues.json word_pops). The three variants rotate in edit order, so two neighbouring words never share a sample. Doc 2.7: 'a soft tick or click at -24 dB'.

whoosh_in.recipe: synthesized (numpy): decorrelated noise through a band-pass (Q 1.2) sweeping 450 Hz -> 3.8 kHz, level swelling as (t/T)^2.4 to its peak at the very end (6 ms release), drifting from left to centre-right; 0.42 s; align END on the key word's frame
whoosh_in.notes: Key/hero words (cues.json key_words): ends on the word's entry frame, the thump starts there. Doc 2.7: 'a short whoosh into it plus a low thump at -14 dB': the thump carries the -14, the whoosh sits 2 dB under it (broadband noise reads louder than a low thump at the same peak).

thump_low.recipe: synthesized (numpy): sine with a pitch drop 110 -> 45 Hz (30 ms), decay 90 ms, tanh drive 1.6 (audible harmonics on phones) + a 3 ms low-passed noise click; 0.36 s; align start
thump_low.notes: Key/hero words (cues.json key_words), on the entry frame.

swipe.recipe: synthesized (numpy): decorrelated noise, band-pass centre riding the envelope (0.9 -> 6.1 kHz at the peak), fast rise / slower fall around a peak at 0.12 s, panned left -> right; 0.30 s; align PEAK on the cut
swipe.notes: Hard cuts in the hook (cues.json hook_cuts, B1-B2); the swipe's peak on the cut frame.

siren_whoop.recipe: S02_Siren.mp3 (the plan's S02/S14 slice): 48 kHz, high-pass 300 Hz (FFmpeg, 2-pole), slice 0.5-1.3 s, 10 ms de-click fade-in, 6f fade-out
siren_whoop.notes: Police siren sweep (doc: 0:00 with sub_hit on frame 0, and 0:03.6).

whoosh_flip.recipe: S10_Flip.wav at 48 kHz, leading silence trimmed (1 ms pre-roll)
whoosh_flip.notes: 3D flip / spin whoosh; its peak (about 0.36 s in) on the flip's midpoint.

whip.recipe: S15_23 Whip Hit.wav at 48 kHz, leading silence trimmed, cut at 0.40 s with an 80 ms fade (only 0.2-0.3 s is audible)
whip.notes: Whip-zooms; the peak on the whip's midpoint.

rewind.recipe: S17_Spinback (2).wav at 48 kHz (= the plan's S17), leading silence trimmed

riser.recipe: S18_Riser Faster.wav at 48 kHz (= the plan's S18), ends at its peak
riser.notes: Short riser; its end on the hit frame.

reverse_cymbal.recipe: synthesized (numpy): decorrelated L/R high-passed noise ring-modulated by five inharmonic partials (3.15-8.2 kHz) = crash colour, under a reversed exponential decay (tau 320 ms, peak at the end) and a low-pass opening 1.5 -> 14 kHz; 1.3 s; align END on the reveal
reverse_cymbal.notes: Doc 2.7: 'a reverse-cymbal riser into each big reveal (31.5 s, 53.0 s, 1:15.5)': ends ON its frame.

keyboard_clatter.recipe: 8 single keystrokes sliced from S13_v3) Type (A B C ).wav (onsets [0.089, 0.182, 0.354, 0.448, 0.533, 0.651, 0.814, 0.915] s) re-sequenced over 2.0 s: gaps 55-140 ms (+180 ms pauses 12% of the time), per-stroke level -4..0 dB, random stroke order (seed 3001), 150 ms fade-out
keyboard_clatter.notes: Typing bed under the CRT (doc: 4.5-6.4 s); 2.0 s, shorten with dur_f.

type_on.recipe: 4 keystrokes of S13 (file order) at 0/68/131/205 ms, 0/-2/-1/-3 dB; 0.32 s
type_on.notes: One typed burst (place one per burst of typed text).

click.recipe: synthesized (numpy): mouse click: press (band-passed 2-6 kHz noise, 1.5 ms + a 3.2 kHz 4 ms ring) and release 55 ms later at 60% (3.6 kHz ring); 0.12 s; align start (press on the frame)

sub_hit.recipe: synthesized (numpy): sub sine 72 -> 38 Hz (50 ms), decay 250 ms, tanh drive 2.0 (2nd/3rd harmonics so phones hear it) + an 8 ms low-passed knock; 0.9 s; align start
sub_hit.notes: Sub-bass hit (doc: frame 0 with the siren whoop).

metal_crunch.recipe: synthesized (numpy): a 25 ms noise burst + thinning crackle (450/s, high-passed 1.5 kHz) exciting seven inharmonic metal modes (397/523/1088/1675/2470/3540/4960 Hz, 300-100 ms rings), plus the raw band-passed scrape and a 60 Hz thud, tanh drive 1.5; 0.8 s; align start
metal_crunch.notes: Doc hook beat 4: 'metal crunch on the flip'.

error_chord.recipe: synthesized (numpy): original synthesized alert chord, NOT Microsoft's file: F#4 C5 F5 B5 (stacked tritone / fourth / tritone), each note 5 partials (1, 2, 3, 4.01, 5.02; upper partials decaying faster), 4 ms attack, 150 ms fall to a 60% sustain, release from 0.25 s (350 ms), +-3 cents L/R detune, a 30 ms D7 ping on the attack; 1.0 s
error_chord.notes: Doc 2.7: the Windows 95 'critical stop' chord (7.5 s): an ORIGINAL chord in that role. 03_SFX/S03a_Windows Error.wav is the old S03 error sound; it is not used for this name.

glitch_stutter.recipe: S03b_Glitch, Flicker, Text (14).wav at 48 kHz, leading silence trimmed

glitch_impact.recipe: S08a_Glitch, Impact.wav at 48 kHz (= the plan's S08a, B8's glitch impact)
glitch_impact.notes: The X4 glitch impact (the S08a sound).

stamp_thud.recipe: synthesized (numpy): rubber stamp on paper on a desk: 85 -> 55 Hz thud (70 ms), a 10 ms band-passed (0.6-2.5 kHz) slap, a 180 Hz desk resonance (60 ms) and a 6 ms paper tick (3-8 kHz), tanh drive 1.4; 0.6 s; align start

impact_boom.recipe: S01_Cinematic Hit 1.wav at 48 kHz, trimmed to 2.5 s with a 20f fade (its tail fills the 0.4 s logo silence)
impact_boom.notes: Big impact (doc: on 'Grand Theft Auto' 53.5 s, with sub_drop); its peak on the slam frame.

sub_drop.recipe: S09_Sub Drop.mp3 decoded by FFmpeg at 48 kHz (encoder delay skipped), trimmed to 2.5 s with a 20f fade (the plan's S09 trim)

paper_rip.recipe: synthesized (numpy): dense noise grains (15 samples each, Poisson rate 600 -> 1500/s, a louder snap cluster at 0.40-0.44 s) band-passed 0.9-6 kHz over a band-passed noise body (0.4-3 kHz, -12 dB), 20 ms attack, 80 ms release; 0.55 s; align start

flatline_beep.recipe: synthesized (numpy): monitor flat-line tone: 1 kHz sine + 8% 3rd harmonic, steady, 8 ms attack/release; 1.2 s (a cue can shorten it with dur_f)

ding.recipe: synthesized (numpy): small bell: E6 (1318.5 Hz) with bell partials 1/2/2.76/5.4 (decays 0.9/0.5/0.35/0.15 s) + a 2 ms strike noise; 1.2 s; align start

hit.recipe: S06a/S06b/S06c (the plan's stamp hits) decoded by FFmpeg at 48 kHz, leading silence trimmed, cut at 0.8 s with an 8f fade (the plan's S06 trim), loudness-matched (max 100 ms K-weighted energy)
hit.notes: Short hits (doc: 'ram.', 'chase.', 'let go.'); 'hit' rotates hit_1 -> hit_2 -> hit_3 in edit order, 'hit_2' picks one; the peak on the frame.
